 O R D E R

As it was found concurrently by both the Trial Court and the High Court that the appellant was guilty of the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954, we are not inclined to interfere with the sentence, particularly, after going through the judgments rendered by them.

However, taking note of para 3 of a judgment of this Court relied upon by the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant in N. Sukumaran Nair v. Food Inspector  (1997) 9 SCC 101, wherein it was stated as follows:
3. The offence took place in the year 1984.

sentences.text: The appellant has been awarded six months' simple imprisonment and has been ordered to pay a fine of Rs. 1000/- under Clause (d) of Reason: Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, "the appropriate Government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
We think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

We, therefore, direct the appellant to deposit in the trial Court a sum of Rupees 6000/- as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months' simple imprisonment within a period of six weeks from today and intimate to the appropriate Government that such fine has been deposited.

On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the Hemantkumar Pradyuman Modi vs M.G.Shaikh Food Inspector on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87478378/
1 matter by passing appropriate orders under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

sentences.text: Upon the appellant depositing a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards commutation of the sentence along with the fine of Rs.1000/- already ordered by the Trial Court, within a period of six weeks from today, and after due intimation to the Government, the State Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders under Clause (d) of Section 474 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (corresponding to Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973).
Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part.
